description: THE GOAL, stated so a change can be judged against it (item #218, 2026-08-22). Renovate exists
to keep the dependency surface patched enough that this repository's OWN gates (SAST/SCA/Trivy)
stay green before a human notices, while never auto-merging and never swamping the single CI
runner. THREE CHANNELS, THREE CADENCES. (1) SECURITY — vulnerabilityAlerts + OSV, schedule-EXEMPT,
runs on the nightly cron, unbudgeted: a known-vulnerable dep gets a PR within a day. (2) LOCKFILE
REFRESH — lockFileMaintenance, the Friday window, but RANKED AHEAD of routine work, because it is
the only channel that clears a CVE finding the manifest range already permits. (3) ROUTINE — base
images, Actions, Cargo, Python, non-RN npm; the Friday window, on a budget.
AND THE REQUIREMENT THAT WAS MISSING UNTIL #218: the routine queue must DRAIN. Throughput has to
exceed arrival, or the tail is not deferred — it is INVISIBLE, and nothing reports it. Because
there is one in-window run per week, prHourlyLimit IS that weekly throughput; prConcurrentLimit is
the deliberate backstop bounding review debt, and must stay above it or it binds first and the
hourly budget can never be spent. renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts both.
Scoped, security-leaning Renovate config for the mcm monorepo (drafted 2026-07-05).
Every Renovate PR runs the normal guardrails + app-ci gates; cd-deploy only fires on merge
to main, so nothing auto-deploys. Nothing is auto-merged — review + let CI gate.
The high-value slice is base-image + Actions + Cargo + Python patching (pairs with the Trivy
gate in cd-deploy). React Native / Expo is deliberately NOT bumped by Renovate (see below).
SCHEDULE (widened 2026-08-13, feature 057 / item #153): the window is THREE hours wide, not one,
and that width is load-bearing rather than slack. Actions cron is UTC-only and does not observe
DST, so renovate.yml's Friday `0 7 * * 5` is 03:00 EDT but 02:00 EST. The previous `* 3 * * 5`
caught only the summer half — and in fact caught neither, because the only cron then was the
nightly 03:00 UTC, which is 23:00 THURSDAY here. The sets never intersected and every routine
update deferred for four weeks with nothing reporting it. `2-4` covers both offsets with an hour
either side. scripts/__tests__/renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts the intersection under
BOTH offsets and fails if this key and that cron ever drift apart again.
NO CUSTOM MANAGER FOR pnpm-workspace.yaml, and this is a MEASURED decision, not an omission
(feature 057 / item #152, T022). The premise it was planned on turned out to be false. Item #152
and the 057 research both assert Renovate extracts ZERO dependencies from pnpm-workspace.yaml.
It does not: run 1704 (2026-08-13) extracted TWELVE from it via the BUILT-IN npm manager, and the
Dependency Dashboard that run wrote lists all ten keyed override floors with pending updates for
five of them. So there is no zero to improve on, and a second manager over a file the npm manager
already reads would double-manage it — two depNames for one package, two branches, both editing
the same lines.
What the built-in manager CANNOT do is the half the story actually cared about. It parses
`fast-uri@<3.1.4` as an opaque DEPNAME and `>=3.1.4 <4` as the version, so it rewrites the value
and leaves the vulnerable-range key stale. Every floor RAISE it proposes is therefore a half-bump
by construction, and Renovate has no mechanism for rewriting a depName. Suppressing the built-in
manager to hand the file to a regex manager would be a far larger, riskier change than the one
that was scoped, and would also drop postcss/@expo/dom-webview/react-dom extraction.
So the guard is the deliverable, not the manager: check-override-consistency.mjs runs on pull
requests and fails a half-bumped proposal by name. The accepted cost is that a bot-authored floor
raise arrives RED and needs its key half fixed by hand — visible and cheap, versus a silent
half-remediation that still looks correct.
ITEM #184 RESOLVED (feature 058, 2026-08-13) ACROSS TWO DIFFERENT FAULTS. Do not conflate them —
the item was originally filed against the first and the SECOND is what actually cost ten days.
FAULT 1, 'the bot cannot propose a floor RAISE' (the half-bump, everything above). DECISION:
ACCEPT, and repair the key half by hand on each bot PR. check-override-consistency.mjs fails a
half-bump by name on every pull request, so nothing unsafe can merge; every override bump in the
git log so far was hand-written anyway; and the alternative — suppressing the built-in npm manager
for this file to hand it to a regex manager — is a materially larger, riskier change that would
also drop postcss/@expo/dom-webview/react-dom extraction. Rejected on those measured grounds.
FAULT 2, 'the bot proposes NOTHING because the range already permits the fix' (the stale lockfile).
DECISION: FIX, two ways — `lockFileMaintenance` below refreshes within existing ranges on a
schedule, and check-sast-findings.mjs now names which lever clears a finding (refresh the lockfile,
or raise both halves of the floor) instead of leaving the reader to work it out. That message is
advisory ONLY and cannot change the gate's exit code; see scripts/override-lever.mjs.
The two faults have different fixes and only the second was load-bearing: options 1-3 in the item
address the half-bump and would NOT have caught the fast-uri case at all.
Open PRs for known-vulnerable deps promptly (the actual security value; complements the SAST/Trivy gates).
osvVulnerabilityAlerts (above) is REQUIRED here: this runs on Forgejo, which has no GitHub-style
advisory API, so native vulnerabilityAlerts alone would be inert — OSV is the working source and
matches what `pnpm audit` / the SAST gate flag.
minimumReleaseAge is dropped to 1 day (vs the 3-day global supply-chain cooldown): a targeted
security patch from an existing dep should remediate FAST — the churn this codifies against was CVEs
sitting un-fixed for days while every PR's SAST/Trivy gate went red (fast-uri/brace-expansion/js-yaml/
shell-quote/axios/tar, 2026-07). 1 day still clears the initial compromised-release window (feature 034).
Feature 058 / item #184. THE FAULT THIS FIXES is not that the bot half-bumps an override — that
is the second-order one, recorded in the top-level description. It is that the bot proposes
NOTHING when an override range ALREADY PERMITS a published fix, because it only proposes when the
current range does not satisfy the newest version, and it reasons about the MANIFEST RANGE rather
than the lockfile resolution. An override whose range permits the fix looks already-fixed to it
while the lockfile stays pinned below.
MEASURED TWICE IN ONE AFTERNOON (2026-08-13). fast-uri: override `>=3.1.4 <4` permitted 3.1.5,
lockfile pinned 3.1.4; fix published 2026-07-31, advisory 2026-08-03 — the fix PREDATED the
advisory by three days and the range already allowed it. The sast gate went red and stayed red
for TEN DAYS, and a four-week allowlist acceptance was written, for something a lockfile refresh
would have cleared. nanoid: same shape, and it reddened main. Confirmation that this is structural
rather than bad luck — all five override updates the dashboard listed were UPPER-bound widenings
(`<4`->`<5`, `<7`->`<9`), never floor raises. Renovate will essentially never raise the lower
bound of one of these.
THE SCHEDULE KEY BELOW IS LOAD-BEARING AND MUST NOT BE DELETED AS REDUNDANT. It looks like a
duplicate of the top-level `schedule` and is not: verified against renovate@44.29.3's own config
resolver, this option's DEFAULT object already carries `schedule: [before 4am on monday]`, and a
child config's value beats the inherited top-level key. Measured — top-level schedule plus
`lockFileMaintenance: {enabled: true}` resolves to [before 4am on monday], NOT to the top-level
window. That default is Monday 04:00-08:00 UTC under EDT and 05:00-09:00 under EST, while
renovate.yml's crons are `0 3 * * *` and `0 7 * * 5`. NEITHER intersects under EITHER offset, so
enabling this without its own window yields a setting that is ON and can NEVER FIRE, reporting
nothing — #153 exactly, the fault feature 057 existed to fix, in a new place.
renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts both halves and fails if this key is removed or drifts.
CADENCE, CORRECTED 2026-08-22 (item #218). This paragraph previously read "a crowded-out refresh
defers a week". That was false, and load-bearingly so: across 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-21 the bot
ran INSIDE its window twice and lockFileMaintenance produced no branch either time. The only
lock-file PR that has ever existed (#199) came from a human ticking unlimit-branch on the
Dependency Dashboard. Two mechanisms in renovate@44's own dist, verified byte-identical from
44.30.3 (which created #199) to 44.39.2: process/sort.js hard-codes sortOrder as pin, digest,
patch, minor, major, lockFileMaintenance — so this channel is processed LAST, behind even majors;
and global/limits.js handleConcurrentLimits() checks the hourly PR limit FIRST for EVERY key, so
spending prHourlyLimit also makes isLimitReached('Branches') true and update/branch/index.js:148
returns 'branch-limit-reached' BEFORE the branch is created. A crowded-out refresh therefore
leaves NOTHING behind, and the nightly runs cannot resume it — they return 'not-scheduled' at
:244 before branch creation too. It did not defer a week; it deferred for ever. The fix is the
prPriority rule in packageRules — NOT a key here, see below — plus a prHourlyLimit that reaches
past the two rolling groups.
The nightly schedule-EXEMPT run still handles urgent security advisories. PAIRED WITH item #186
(feature 058): a lockfile-only PR now runs app-e2e, so these
weekly refreshes are end-to-end tested rather than merged on the strength of the light jobs — 057
FR-013, `nx test` passes straight over a broken transitive floor.
Keep nx.json's `installation.version` in lockstep with package.json's `nx` devDependency.
Renovate only sees package.json, so an nx bump used to land as a HALF bump: PR #141 raised
package.json to 22.7.7 and left nx.json at 22.7.2. The Nx WRAPPER wins at runtime, so every
`pnpm nx` — and all of CI — would have kept running 22.7.2 and the SECURITY UPDATE THE PR
EXISTED FOR would not have taken effect. check-toolchain-consistency.mjs catches it and reds
the `naming` job, which is how it was found; this manager stops it being proposed at all.
THIS MANAGER ALONE DOES NOT MAKE BOTH FILES MOVE TOGETHER. The comment that used to stand
here — 'Both files therefore move in one PR' — was FALSE for as long as it stood, and being
asserted rather than tested is what made the defect invisible (item #194). Measured on PR #193
(2026-08-14): it arrived bumping nx.json to 22.7.8 and leaving package.json on 22.7.7 — the
mirror image of #141, same pair, other half. EXTRACTION IS NOT GROUPING.
MECHANISM: this manager's manager is `custom.regex`, NOT `npm` (renovate@44 ManagersMatcher
matches custom managers as `custom.${manager}`). `group:monorepos`, pulled in by
config:recommended, puts BOTH halves in an `nx monorepo` group by matchSourceUrls. The
`js patch/minor` and `js majors` rules below then match `matchManagers: ["npm"]` and, because
LATER packageRules override earlier ones, pull ONLY the package.json half back out — onto
`renovate/js-patchminor` while the nx.json half stayed on `renovate/nx-monorepo`. Two branches.
WHAT ACTUALLY HOLDS THEM TOGETHER is the explicit `nx monorepo` packageRule below, which matches
BOTH managers and is ordered AFTER those two rules so it wins, on the major track as well as
patch/minor. Do not remove this manager without also removing that gate, and do not delete or
reorder that rule — renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs fails by name if either moves.
Keep the Playwright CONTAINER IMAGE tag in app-ci.yml in lockstep with the @playwright/test
version pnpm-lock.yaml resolves. Item #204, measured on PR #199 (2026-08-15): a lock-file
maintenance PR moved the lockfile 1.60.0 -> 1.62.1 and left BOTH image pins at
v1.60.0-noble. The tag selects the BAKED BROWSER BUILD, so the runner looked for an
executable the image does not carry and ZERO TESTS RAN. It did not fail the suite — it
produced no counts at all (`[e2e-gate] failed=0 flaky=0 passed=0`), which the result gate
caught only after a full ~35-minute app-e2e cycle and only as a generic 'app-e2e failed'.
NOTHING EXTRACTED THIS TAG BEFORE. Measured with `RENOVATE_PLATFORM=local
RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=extract`: app-ci.yml is matched by the `github-actions` manager ONLY, and
that manager reads `uses:` and container:/services: images — not an image inside a `run:`
shell block. So the lockfile half moved on a schedule and the tag half moved by hand.
EXTRACTION IS NOT GROUPING. This entry alone does NOT make both files move together — the
`playwright pin` packageRule below is what does, and it must stay ordered after the broad
`js patch/minor` / `js majors` rules. That distinction is not theoretical: the nx pair had
this exact manager for months and still half-bumped twice (PR #141, PR #193) because a
later npm rule pulled its lockfile half back out. Do not delete that rule as redundant.
THE npm DATASOURCE IS DELIBERATE, not a shortcut. It gives both halves ONE depName, so a
single matchPackageNames re-joins them; it keeps the tag out of `docker:pinDigests`, which
would rewrite the literal string that scripts/__tests__/app-e2e-env.guard.test.mjs locates
the docker run by; and it keeps it out of the `docker base images` group, which would file
Playwright alongside Postgres and Keycloak rather than with its own runner.
ACCEPTED RESIDUAL RISK: npm can publish @playwright/test@X before
mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:vX-noble exists, so a proposed tag can 404. That is accepted
because it fails LOUDLY — `docker run` exits on `manifest unknown` and reds the job — which
is the opposite of the silent zero-test run this whole entry exists to remove. Trading a
loud failure for a silent one is the point. Revisit only if a publication lag actually
bites; the docker-datasource alternative was rejected on the three grounds above.
check-toolchain-consistency.mjs fails a drifted pin in ~0.4s regardless, so a bot that
somehow moves one half still cannot merge.
Keep the pinned Trivy version current in BOTH workflows that install it. Item #303.
WHAT WAS WRONG. Both installs fetched the install script from the MOVING branch `main` and
piped it into sh, then passed NO tag — and the script's own usage says 'If tag is missing,
then the latest will be used'. Two floating references on one line, in the tool that decides
whether a Critical blocks a deploy, with NO digest pin underneath. Strictly worse than the
infra images item #297 fixed: docker:pinDigests at least made those reproducible while
unclassifiable; this had neither property.
THE COST WAS PAID IMMEDIATELY, during #297. The local sweep that produced the stale-
suppression evidence ran aquasec/trivy:0.74.0 while CI ran an unknown version, so two scans
of BYTE-IDENTICAL images could not be compared with confidence — purely because one side's
scanner had no version to name.
WHY THIS MANAGER EXISTS AT ALL. A pin with nothing maintaining it trades a floating
reference for a ROTTING one — the failure mode feature 063's research R3 had to rule out by
hand for minio. Trivy is actively released, so the pin must be maintained. github-releases is
the correct datasource: Trivy ships GitHub releases, not an npm package, and the tag form
(`v0.74.0`) is what both the URL and the positional install argument take.
ONE ASSIGNMENT, TWO USES — deliberately. The version is written once as TRIVY_VERSION and
interpolated into both the script URL and the install tag, so a bump cannot move one and
leave the other. Pinning the script to one release while installing a different one is a pin
that does not say what it means — the half-bump shape #194/#204/#225 already record.
EXTRACTION IS NOT GROUPING (same caveat as the Playwright entry above). This manager makes
the version VISIBLE to Renovate; it does not by itself keep the two FILES in step. The guard
in renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts the RESOLVED state — both pinned, both agreeing,
the script ref equal to the installed tag, and this manager's matchStrings actually capturing
a currentValue in each file. A manager whose regex misses is indistinguishable from no
manager at all, which is how the nx half-bump survived review twice.
Keep frontend/mcm-app/Dockerfile's `corepack prepare pnpm@<version>` pins in lockstep with
package.json's `packageManager`. Renovate manages the manifest field and has no visibility of the
Dockerfile, so every bot-authored pnpm bump arrived as a HALF BUMP and failed
check-toolchain-consistency.mjs by construction — item #225.
MEASURED TWICE. PR #217 (2026-08-21) moved packageManager to pnpm@11.22.0 and left both Dockerfile
lines at 11.17.0. PR #263 (2026-08-28) moved it to 11.24.0 and left both at 11.22.0, reddening
`guardrails / naming` on a branch Renovate REGENERATES weekly — so it re-blocked on that schedule.
THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE, and the second Renovate produces: nx (item #194, package.json vs
nx.json) and Playwright (item #204, lockfile vs the image tag in app-ci.yml) are the two above.
EXTRACTION IS NOT GROUPING — the lesson both of those recorded the hard way. This entry alone does
NOT make the halves move together; the `pnpm pin` packageRule below is what does, and it must stay
ordered after the broad `js patch/minor` / `js majors` rules. The nx pair carried a customManager
for months and still half-bumped twice (PR #141, PR #193) because a later npm rule pulled its
manifest half back out.
SCOPED TO THE DOCKERFILE BY NAME, deliberately. docs/runbooks/dev-environment-setup.md also says
`corepack prepare pnpm@latest`, which is prose for a human and not a pin — the toolchain gate's own
PINNED_FILES list excludes it for the same reason, and a broader pattern would file `latest` as a
version and propose bumps against documentation.
UNVERIFIED AND FLAGGED: the file carries the version on TWO byte-identical lines (build stage and
runtime stage). Whether Renovate rewrites both, or only the first, is not established here — see
item #225 for the check to run on the first bot-authored pnpm bump after this lands, and for the
ARG-single-sourcing fallback if it turns out to rewrite only one. The toolchain gate still fails
closed either way, so the worst case is the status quo, not a silent half-bump.
Item #307 — the DEVCONTAINER half of the Rust pin. rust-toolchain.toml itself needs no
manager: renovate@44 ships a BUILT-IN `rust-toolchain` manager (managerFilePatterns
`/(^|/)rust-toolchain(\.toml)?$/`) emitting depName `rust` on the `rust-version` datasource,
and a second manager over the same file would double-manage it — two depNames for one
package, two branches, both editing the same line, which is precisely why this config
declines to add a regex manager over pnpm-workspace.yaml.
The devcontainer image bakes its own copy because it is built BEFORE the repository exists,
so it cannot read the toolchain file. Same depName AND same datasource on purpose: that is
what makes the two halves ONE dependency rather than two that happen to share a name. The
`rust toolchain` packageRule below is what actually keeps them in one branch —
EXTRACTION IS NOT GROUPING (#194, #204, #225).
Item #307 — semgrep. `SEMGREP_PIN` was already pinned and extracted by NOTHING (confirmed
against a local Renovate extract: zero semgrep depNames), which is a ROTTING pin: item
#303's principle is that a pin with nothing maintaining it merely trades a floating
reference for a stale one. It is installed as `uvx semgrep@<pin>`, hence PyPI.
One file, one manager, one depName — so no grouping rule is needed here. Grouping is
required when a SECOND manager sees the other half (nx, Playwright, pnpm, uv below); it is
not a ritual to perform on every custom manager. The Trivy manager above is the precedent:
two files, one depName, no group, one branch.
Item #307 — cargo-audit, the tool that decides whether a Rust advisory blocks the merge.
It was installed as `cargo install cargo-audit --locked`, i.e. LATEST every run: `--locked`
locks the crate's DEPENDENCIES, not the crate's own version. The devcontainer installed it
unpinned too, so a local scan and the CI scan of identical inputs could disagree — the cost
item #303 measured for Trivy.
Two files, two spellings (`--version X` in the workflow, `cargo-audit@X` in the image), one
depName on the crates.io datasource — so one dependency in one branch, no grouping rule.
Item #307 — uv, and THE DECISION ABOUT ITS SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH, which item #308 consumes.
uv had three install shapes and none was pinned: two `curl astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` in
guardrails, one in the devcontainer image (a MOVING script piped to sh — byte-for-byte the
shape #303 removed for Trivy), and five `astral-sh/setup-uv` steps whose ACTION was
digest-pinned while the uv it installs resolved latest at run time. uv is pre-1.0, moves
fast, and is the GENERATOR for the uv.lock files the weekly lockFileMaintenance channel
merges — a generator-version change can alter lockfile output in the one workflow whose
output merges weekly.
THE DECISION: uv's single source of truth is ONE VERSION STRING, repeated at every site,
held together by this ONE customManager plus the `uv pin` packageRule below, and asserted
equal across every site by renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs. It is deliberately NOT a file
that every site reads: `astral-sh/setup-uv`'s `version:` input is an Actions expression and
cannot read a repository file, so a file would leave the five action sites unpinned — the
half-measure that produces exactly the drift this fixes. The nx/Playwright/pnpm pins are the
precedent for the shape (one string, many sites, one guard).
ITEM #308 CONSUMES THIS: the eight `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest@sha256:…` image refs re-tag
to `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:<this version>`, which the BUILT-IN docker manager sees under a
different depName and a different datasource. That is why `uv pin` below matches both — the
group is wired now so #308 is a re-tag rather than a re-think.
The `# uv-version` marker on the action inputs is load-bearing: without it the matchString
would be a bare `version:` key and would claim any other `version:` input added to those
workflows later.
Item #218 — rank the lockfile refresh AHEAD of routine updates. Renovate sorts
lockFileMaintenance LAST of all update types (process/sort.js), and the two rolling groups
(cargo deps, js patch/minor) regenerate every week and sort ahead of it, so with one in-window
run per week it was never reached — measured 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-21, both in-window, zero
lock-file branches created.
THIS KEY BELONGS HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE. prPriority is declared parents:[packageRules], so
setting it inside the lockFileMaintenance block looks correct and Renovate simply ignores it.
renovate-config-validator DOES report that (WARN, exit 1 — measured), and since item #309 it
RUNS IN CI: `guardrails / renovate-config` validates this file --strict --no-global on every
pull request, and renovate.yml validates it again with the same major before the weekly run
acts on it. The guard test still asserts the absence of the wrong placement, because the two
catch different things — the validator catches a key Renovate does not know, the guard test
catches a key it knows but ignores HERE. It works from HERE because updates/flatten.js sets
updateType=lockFileMaintenance BEFORE calling applyPackageRules, and generateBranchConfig then
spreads upgrades[0] onto the branch, which is what sortBranches reads.
It must NOT be narrowed by matchPackageNames either: a lockFileMaintenance
upgrade is built with no dep attached, so such a rule would match nothing and never fire.
5 rather than 1 leaves room to rank something above it later without renumbering.

packageRules.description: Supply-chain cooldown (feature 034): hold every update until the release is ≥3 days old, mitigating the compromised-just-published-release window. Applies globally via a catch-all match.

Never bump our OWN registry images — cd-deploy owns those digests (digest-by-git promotion). Matched by the jumbleknot namespace, NOT the forge host literal (topology-scrub gate forbids the host in git).

React Native / Expo are version-locked: Expo SDK + RN upgrades MUST go through `expo install` / the expo upgrade skill, not raw Renovate bumps, or the mobile build breaks in subtle ways. Disable the RN/Expo core in the app package.

React is version-locked to the Expo SDK across the WHOLE workspace, not just the app. react/react-dom also live in the root package.json and packages/design-system — the previous app-only ignore let Renovate bump those two, splitting React (root/design-system ahead of the Expo-pinned app). A split React = two physical copies = invalid-hook-call at runtime. Disable react/react-dom/react-test-renderer repo-wide so they only ever move together via the expo upgrade skill.

description: React NATIVE is version-locked repo-wide for the same reason as react/react-dom above, and it
was LEFT BEHIND when that fix was made — the rule that locks it is matchFileNames-scoped to
frontend/mcm-app/package.json, while react-native also lives in packages/design-system.
MEASURED 2026-08-21, PR #217: react-native 0.85.3 -> 0.87.0 arrived via design-system. RN 0.87
narrowed the press-event type, so GestureResponderEvent stopped satisfying Tamagui's
PressableProps['onPress'] — 15 typecheck errors across 14 files.
THE `/^react-native-/` PATTERN IS THE SECOND HALF AND IS NOT REDUNDANT. The app-scoped rule
lists `react-native` and `/^@react-native//` but nothing matching react-native-reanimated,
react-native-worklets, gesture-handler, screens or safe-area-context — all of which the Expo
SDK pins in its own version matrix, and all five of which #217 also bumped. They were never
locked ANYWHERE, not even in the app.
renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts the resolved `enabled` for this family in EVERY
workspace manifest, because a rule that merely MENTIONS react-native passed the old check.
The EXPO SDK COMPANION packages are version-locked repo-wide. This is the THIRD instance of
one scope defect, after react/react-dom and react-native above, and it is the widest: the
app-scoped rule two above lists `expo`, `/^expo-/` and `/^@expo//`, and NONE of those three
patterns matches a companion that carries no expo prefix at all. babel-preset-expo,
jest-expo and eslint-config-expo were therefore locked NOWHERE — not in the app either.
The `/^@expo//` half was locked only inside frontend/mcm-app/package.json, while
@expo/dom-webview is declared in pnpm-workspace.yaml, which that rule does not reach.
MEASURED 2026-08-27 from the Dependency Dashboard (item #29). The `js majors` group was
holding babel-preset-expo ~56.0.14 -> ~57.0.0, jest-expo ~56.0.4 -> ~57.0.0,
eslint-config-expo ~56.0.4 -> ~57.0.0 and @expo/dom-webview ^56.0.5 -> ^57.0.0, while `expo`
itself sat at ^56.0.8 and react-native at 0.85.3 — both correctly disabled. Taking that
group would have left an SDK-56 RUNTIME running SDK-57 BUILD AND TEST TOOLING. That is a
worse failure than the RN one it rhymes with: babel-preset-expo compiles the app bundle and
jest-expo supplies the jest preset, so the halves that move are the TRANSFORM and the TEST
ENVIRONMENT, which fail as unexplained transform errors rather than as typecheck errors
pointing at a dependency.
NOT matchFileNames-scoped, deliberately. eslint-config-expo and jest-expo also live in
packages/design-system/package.json — the exact manifest react-native escaped through in
PR #217 — and @expo/dom-webview lives in pnpm-workspace.yaml. An app-scoped lock would miss
both, which is the whole defect being fixed here.
`/-expo$/` is the forward-looking half and is what covers the three unprefixed companions.
It is written as a suffix pattern rather than three literals because the SDK names its
companions by suffix, so the next one arrives already locked rather than after an incident.
@expo-google-fonts/* is deliberately NOT matched and must stay updatable: it is not pinned
to the SDK matrix, and no pattern here reaches it — `/^@expo//` requires a SLASH after
`@expo`, while the font packages separate with a HYPHEN.
Upgrades to any of this family go through `expo install` / the expo upgrade skill together
with `expo` and `react-native`, never a raw Renovate bump.
renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts the resolved `enabled` for this family in EVERY
workspace manifest, pnpm-workspace.yaml included, for the same reason it does for RN: a rule
that merely MENTIONS expo passed the old check.

packageRules.description: Group Docker base-image updates into one PR per image (postgres, keycloak, mongo, opensearch, vault, node, caddy, langfuse, clickhouse…). This is the main security win.

description: A 0.x crate's MINOR bump is a semver-MAJOR in effect, but Renovate classifies it as `minor`,
so it rides in the routine `cargo deps` group above. This rule must stay AFTER that one: the
last matching rule wins the groupName.
MEASURED 2026-08-21, PR #216. base64 0.22 -> 0.23 and reqwest 0.12 -> 0.13 arrived as routine.
reqwest 0.13 feature-gated RequestBuilder::form, so every mc-service integration TEST TARGET
stopped compiling — and `mc-service-checks` went green anyway, because it does not build them;
only app-e2e caught it, as an opaque step failure. reqwest 0.13 also added a SECOND reqwest to
the graph alongside the 0.12.28 that axum-keycloak-auth pulls, which backend/mc-service/
Cargo.toml's own dev-dependency comment explicitly forbids. base64 0.23 could not REPLACE
0.22.1 either — bson, mongodb, jsonwebtoken, hyper-util and axum all still require it — so it
only duplicated the crate.
dependencyDashboardApproval keeps these OFF the weekly PR budget (item #218) until a human asks
for one. Grouping alone would not help: a breaking upgrade cannot be made green by config, so
without approval it simply arrives red every week and crowds out the genuinely routine bumps.

packageRules.description: Non-app JS/TS deps (scripts, mcm-app NON-RN deps, workspace tooling): majors separate + never auto-merged.

Non-app JS/TS patch + minor updates grouped into ONE PR to cut churn — the majors rule above long CLAIMED this but no rule implemented it, so each npm patch/minor opened its own PR. Majors stay separate (rule above); the RN/Expo/react disables above still win (they set enabled:false and this rule doesn't override that).

description: nx MOVES AS ONE UNIT — item #194. nx lives in TWO files: package.json's `nx` devDependency
(built-in `npm` manager) and nx.json's `installation.version` (the customManagers regex entry
above, whose manager is `custom.regex`). The Nx WRAPPER wins at runtime, so if only one half
moves the manifest is fiction: PR #141 moved package.json and not nx.json, PR #193 moved
nx.json and not package.json, and check-toolchain-consistency.mjs correctly reds the `naming`
job on both shapes.
config:recommended's `group:monorepos` already groups both halves as `nx monorepo`. The two
`matchManagers: ["npm"]` rules ABOVE were splitting that apart, because a customManager is not
the npm manager and later rules override earlier ones. THIS RULE MUST THEREFORE STAY LAST of
the three: it re-joins both halves by matching BOTH managers, and it deliberately carries no
matchUpdateTypes so it also covers the MAJOR track (nx v23 split identically —
`major-js-majors-(review-individually)` vs `major-nx-monorepo`). Major and minor still get
their own branches via the standard `major-` branch prefix; what is shared is the GROUP.
Verified against renovate@44's own package-rule matcher, not by reading the docs.
THE `@nx/` PATTERN IS NOT PADDING. The root package.json also carries @nx/expo and
@nx/playwright, which `group:monorepos` puts in this same group by sourceUrl and which the two
npm rules above pull out alongside `nx` itself. Grouping ONLY `nx` would fix the nx.json half
and split the Nx CORE from its PLUGINS instead — core in `nx monorepo`, plugins in
`js patch/minor`, two PRs — trading one skew for another. All of them move together.
PLAYWRIGHT MOVES AS ONE UNIT — item #204, the same shape as the nx rule above and for the
same measured reason. @playwright/test lives in pnpm-lock.yaml (built-in `npm` manager) and
the mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v<x>-noble tag lives in app-ci.yml (the customManagers
regex entry above, manager `custom.regex`). The tag selects the baked browser build, so a
PR that moves only the lockfile runs ZERO tests and reports no counts at all — PR #199,
~35 minutes to surface, and it presented as a generic 'app-e2e failed'.
THIS RULE MUST STAY AFTER `js patch/minor` AND `js majors`. Both match
matchManagers: ["npm"], a customManager's manager is `custom.regex`, and LATER rules
override earlier ones — so placed any earlier, those two would pull the lockfile half back
out onto its own branch and leave the tag half alone. That is exactly how the nx pair
half-bumped on PR #141 and PR #193, from the manager that existed to prevent it.
NO matchUpdateTypes, deliberately: restricting it would let at least one track fall through
to the broad npm rules, and the major track splits identically to patch/minor.
THE EXACT NAME, NEVER A /playwright/ PATTERN. A substring match would also capture
@nx/playwright and steal it from the `nx monorepo` group — splitting the Nx core from its
own plugins, i.e. trading one skew for another. renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts
both halves share a group on all three tracks, that this rule matches BOTH managers and is
ordered last, and — as the control — that @nx/playwright still lands in `nx monorepo`.
@copilotkit/* SHIPS BREAKING CHANGES IN MINOR BUMPS, so it must not ride `js patch/minor` — the
group whose whole premise is that a human skims it and merges. Same defect as the cargo 0.x rule
above, with a version number that does not advertise it: there, a 0.x MINOR is a semver-major and
the version string says so; here the package is past 1.0 and the minor looks routine.
MEASURED 2026-08-28, PR #263 (item #265). @copilotkit/react-native 1.67.1 -> 1.69.0 and
@copilotkit/runtime 1.59.5 -> 1.69.0 arrived as routine patch/minor and broke two ways at once:
the `useRenderToolRegistry` export was REMOVED (TS2305, plus `is not a function` at runtime in
assistant-dock.tsx:150), and generative-UI `render({ args })` began passing PARTIAL args so a
render can draw mid-stream — which stopped four components typechecking where they spread args
into props with required fields.
THE COST IS NOT THE MIGRATION, IT IS THE BLAST RADIUS. PR #263 also carried @ai-sdk/openai and
pnpm, both routine. One breaking member makes the whole PR unmergeable and unsplittable, its red
says nothing about the other members, and Renovate REGENERATES the branch weekly — so the routine
bumps stay blocked for as long as the migration takes.
dependencyDashboardApproval keeps these OFF the weekly PR budget (item #218) until a human asks
for one, exactly as for cargo 0.x: a breaking upgrade cannot be made green by config, so without
approval it just arrives red every week and crowds out genuinely routine work.
PATCH IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ROUTINE and matchUpdateTypes is what does it. Two reasons, and the
second is the load-bearing one: nothing measured says a copilotkit PATCH is breaking, and gating
every track would put a SECURITY patch behind a human tick — vulnerabilityAlerts is
schedule-exempt precisely so a known-vulnerable dep gets a PR within a day, and approval-gating it
would take that back. Gate the breaking tracks, leave the remediation track open. This mirrors the
cargo 0.x rule, which also gates `minor` only.
ORDERED LAST, and that is not cosmetic. Later packageRules override earlier ones, so this must sit
AFTER the broad `js patch/minor` and `js majors` rules or they pull it straight back out — the
exact trap that half-bumped the nx pair twice (PR #141, PR #193) and stranded the Playwright tag
(#204). renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts the RESOLVED group, that this rule is the LAST to
group @copilotkit/*, that a major is caught too, that patch is not, and — as the control — that a
routine npm package still lands in `js patch/minor`.
hashicorp/vault IS HELD BELOW 1.19, and this is a SECURITY decision rather than a currency one.
MEASURED 2026-08-30 on PR #289. The `docker base images` group proposed vault 1.18 -> 1.21 and
reddened `infra-image-scan / infra-image-scan`. Scanned with the gate's OWN criteria
(trivy --severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed) against the exact digest the PR pinned:
vault:1.18 — 3 unique fixable Criticals, ALL THREE allowlisted (seed entries):
CVE-2025-68121 (stdlib), CVE-2026-31789 (libcrypto3+libssl3), CVE-2026-33186 (grpc).
vault:1.21 — 4 unique fixable Criticals, NONE suppressed: the libcrypto3 and grpc pair carried
over still unfixed, PLUS NEW CVE-2026-33815 and CVE-2026-33816 in github.com/jackc/pgx/v5.
1.21 DOES clear CVE-2025-68121 (Go retoolchain), so the bump is a net +1 advisory.
TWO independent reasons it went red. (1) The three allowlist entries are keyed to the regex
`hashicorp/vault:1\.18`, which cannot match `hashicorp/vault:1.21@sha256:...`. The matcher in
check-infra-image-findings.mjs is an UNANCHORED `new RegExp(e.image).test(f.image)` — which is
also why appending a digest does NOT break the other entries (`minio/mc`, `grafana/otel-lgtm:latest`
and `opensearchproject/opensearch:2` all still match, verified). (2) The two pgx Criticals are
genuinely new and allowlisted nowhere.
THIS WAS ALREADY MEASURED AND WRITTEN DOWN, by feature 036, in the allowlist justifications the
seed entries carry: 'Bump to 1.21.4 would clear THIS one (Go retoolchained) but NOT the sibling
libcrypto3/grpc Crits, and 1.21.4 adds NEW pgx Criticals (Trivy-verified, feature 036)'. The bump
walked into a documented trap. The standing decision recorded there — 'no fully-clean upstream tag
yet; internal-only + dormant. Re-triage when a clean vault tag ships' — is what this rule now
ENFORCES instead of merely recording.
`allowedVersions` rather than `enabled: false`, deliberately: a DIGEST refresh within 1.18 is still
wanted (docker:pinDigests keeps the pin honest) and only the version move is blocked. Vault also
stays in the `docker base images` group, so its digest is not stranded in a PR of its own.
WIDENING THE ALLOWLIST TO BLESS 1.21 WAS REJECTED. That would make a red gate green by accepting a
strictly worse image — the one thing the allowlist must never be used for (its own header says
suppression is gate-only and the baseline stays visible). LIFT THIS RULE when a vault tag ships
that clears libcrypto3 and grpc without adding pgx; re-scan before believing a release note.
renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts the RESOLVED ceiling on all three tracks, that no other
docker image picks it up, and — as the control — that vault still rides `docker base images`.
pnpm MOVES AS ONE UNIT — item #225, the same requirement as the nx and Playwright rules above and
for the same reason. pnpm's version lives in package.json's `packageManager` (built-in `npm`
manager) and in frontend/mcm-app/Dockerfile's corepack pins (the customManagers entry above, whose
manager is `custom.regex`). If only the manifest half moves, check-toolchain-consistency.mjs reds
`guardrails / naming` and the PR cannot merge.
THIS RULE IS WHAT ACTUALLY HOLDS THEM TOGETHER. The customManager only EXTRACTS. Without this,
`js patch/minor` (matchManagers: [npm]) claims the manifest half and, because later rules override
earlier ones, strands the Dockerfile half on its own branch — exactly how the nx pair half-bumped
twice with its manager already in place (PR #141, PR #193).
ORDERED LAST for that reason. matchUpdateTypes is deliberately UNRESTRICTED so it covers patch,
minor and major alike; restricting it would let one track fall through to the broad npm rules and
half-bump, which is the trap the Playwright rule's own guard test asserts against.
SIDE EFFECT, INTENDED: this takes pnpm OUT of the `js patch/minor` group. A pnpm bump now arrives
as its own PR carrying every half, instead of riding with unrelated packages whose red it would
then be confused with — PR #263 carried exactly that confusion, a pnpm half-bump reddening `naming`
alongside an unrelated CopilotKit break reddening `affected`.
renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts both halves share a group on all three tracks, that this
rule matches BOTH managers and is ordered last, that the customManager still exists and targets the
Dockerfile, and — as the control — that unrelated npm packages still land in `js patch/minor`.
THERE WERE THREE HALVES UNTIL 2026-08-29, NOT TWO — item #286. frontend/mcm-app/package.json carried
its OWN `packageManager`, which this rule silently grouped alongside the root's because the npm manager
extracts the field from EVERY manifest. The migration (a19962b9) wrote pnpm@10.33.0 into both; every
later bump moved the root only, and Renovate maintained the app copy on its own track — 871d79aa took
it 10.33.0 -> 10.34.5 while the root reached 11.22.0, and the dashboard was offering a `pnpm to v11`
MAJOR (`renovate/major-pnpm-pin`) against the shadow copy. That branch is not a real update; it is this
rule correctly grouping a pin that should never have existed.
THE FIELD IS NOW DECLARED ONCE, in the root manifest, and check-toolchain-consistency.mjs FAILS any
non-root package.json that declares it — including one whose value agrees, because corepack and pnpm
resolve `packageManager` from the NEAREST package.json above the cwd, so a second copy silently wins
inside that directory. Do not re-add one to make a workspace package 'self-contained': it re-creates a
second Renovate dependency on a separate major track, which is exactly what went unnoticed for months.
openpolicyagent/opa MOVES AS ONE UNIT, AND ONLY ONTO THE TWO VARIANTS THIS REPOSITORY RUNS.
Feature 063 / item #297. The repository uses TWO tags of ONE dependency: `1.20.1` in
observability/compose.yaml (the OPA sidecar) and `1.20.1-debug` in compose.prod.yaml (the
same build with a shell, for prod triage). That is the ONLY genuine pairing risk among the
eight images this feature pinned: two different tags, two files, one dependency name, and
nothing about the layout forcing them to move together. curl, otel-lgtm, minio, mc and
unleash each carry an IDENTICAL ref in both observability files, so Renovate sees one
dependency with two locations and rewrites both by construction — they need no rule.
`allowedVersions` is a PERMIT-LIST, not a ceiling, and deliberately so. openpolicyagent/opa
publishes 3573 tags including `-dev`, `-rootless`, `-static` and `-static-debug` builds. A
denylist of the suffixes known to be wrong goes stale the moment upstream invents a fourth,
and the pre-release markers FR-006 names (rc/alpha/beta/nightly/snapshot) are open-ended.
Permitting exactly `X.Y.Z` and `X.Y.Z-debug` is closed, so a new variant is excluded by
default rather than by having been predicted.
This does NOT set groupName: opa stays in `docker base images` with everything else, so the
two refs are proposed in one PR rather than stranded on separate branches. That is the half-
bump shape this repository has now paid for four times (#194 nx, #204 Playwright, #225 pnpm,
and the vault allowlist key in PR #289), and in every one of those a mechanism EXISTED that
looked sufficient and was silently overridden by a later, broader rule — which is why
renovate-workflow.guard.test.mjs asserts the RESOLVED group, ceiling and enabled flag on all
three update tracks, that the permit-list accepts both variants in use and rejects `-dev`,
`-rootless`, `-static` and the pre-release markers, and — as the control — that no other
docker image picks the restriction up.
minio/minio AND minio/mc ARE DATE-TAGGED, AND THEIR UPDATE TYPES ARE CALENDAR ARITHMETIC.
Feature 063 / item #297. Both publish `RELEASE.<iso-date>` tags and nothing semver-shaped, so
the two references here are pinned to `RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z` (minio) and
`RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z` (mc) — in both cases the NEWEST tag upstream has published.
The 2025 dates look like neglect and are not: MinIO stopped publishing community releases
after 2025-09, so the floating tag had not been tracking anything for about a year. Do not
'fix' these pins forward; there is nothing ahead of them.
`loose` WAS THE PREFERRED SCHEME AND CANNOT PARSE THESE TAGS AT ALL. Measured against
renovate@44's own dist rather than taken from documentation: modules/versioning/loose matches
on /^[vV]?(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)(.*)$/, so a tag beginning `RELEASE.` fails _parse and returns null.
An unparseable version is not 'ordered without semantics' — it is invisible. `docker`
versioning has the same parse problem. `regex` is the only supported scheme that reads this
shape, and it is present in renovate@44's versioning module list.
THE COST, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN (FR-004). Mapping year->major, month->minor, day->patch
means a January release reports `major` because THE YEAR ADVANCED, not because anything
broke, and any other month reports `minor` for no reason but the calendar. These labels are
orderable but NOT semantic; do not read a `major` here as a risk signal the way you would for
opa or unleash. It satisfies FR-003 mechanically and FR-004 exists because it does not
satisfy it usefully.
THE TRAILING `Z$` ANCHOR IS LOAD-BEARING. The same namespace publishes `-cpuv1` variants
(e.g. RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z-cpuv1); without the anchor Renovate could drift onto one —
the same defect class as opa's `-dev`/`-rootless` tags above.
NO `build` GROUP, DELIBERATELY. renovate@44's regex versioning pushes `build` through
Number.parseInt, so a time component `16-13-09` truncates to `16` and would imply a sub-day
precision the comparison does not have. Date granularity is honest. Residual risk: two
releases on the same calendar day compare equal — MinIO has never done that, and now cannot.
THESE TWO REFERENCES REMAIN DECLARED FLOATING-TAG EXCEPTIONS, BY DESIGN. infra-image-scan.mjs
calls a tag floating when it does not begin with an optional `v` and a digit, so `RELEASE.*`
is still reported `[floating tag]` after this pin. Widening isFloatingTag to recognise the
shape would make the report read clean while teaching a general-purpose classifier to vouch
for an ordering it does not have, and would couple it to one vendor's tag convention — the
move the spec's edge cases forbid. THIS RULE'S matchPackageNames IS THE DECLARED LIST:
infra-image-scan.test.mjs reads it from here and asserts the floating references are EXACTLY
these two — so a ninth floating image fails, and so does a count of ZERO, which would mean
the classifier had been widened to hide them rather than declare them.
Item #307 — hold the two halves of the Rust pin in ONE branch. rust-toolchain.toml is read
by the built-in `rust-toolchain` manager and the devcontainer's baked copy by the custom
manager above; both emit depName `rust` on the `rust-version` datasource. Without this rule
nothing states that they belong together, and this repository has paid three times for
assuming extraction implies grouping (nx #141/#193, Playwright #204, pnpm #225).
matchDatasources is what keeps this OFF backend/mc-service/Dockerfile's `rust:alpine3.21`,
which is depName `rust` on the DOCKER datasource — a different dependency with a different
version grammar, and an ACCEPTED DIVERGENCE (item #307 criterion 1): `alpine3.21` carries no
version, so Renovate can only churn its digest, and re-tagging it is a change under
`backend/`, which is SDD-gated. Recorded rather than done silently.
Ordered last, because a LATER packageRule overrides an earlier one.
Item #307/#308 — hold EVERY uv reference in one branch. The custom manager above sees the
install-script URLs and the setup-uv inputs as `astral-sh/uv` on github-releases; item
#308's re-tagged image refs are seen by the BUILT-IN docker manager as
`ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv` on the docker datasource. Different manager AND different datasource,
so `docker base images` (above) would claim the image half and strand the rest.
The docker packageName is matched HERE, before #308 lands, so that item is a re-tag rather
than a re-think — and so this rule is wrong-and-loud rather than silently absent if the
re-tag ever arrives without it.
Ordered last, after `docker base images` and after the broad js rules, because a LATER
packageRule overrides an earlier one.
NO RELEASE-AGE COOLDOWN FOR uv — DECIDED 2026-09-04 (PR #347), and the null below is the
whole decision. The group half-bumped WITH this rule in place: the eight github-releases sites
moved to 0.12.8, the four ghcr.io image tags stayed at 0.12.7, and the guard test went red.
MECHANISM, from renovate@44.62.0's own dist and a local `RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=lookup`:
`minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour` defaults to `timestamp-required`; the docker datasource has a
releaseTimestamp ONLY for Docker Hub (`tag_last_pushed`), so under ANY cooldown a ghcr.io tag
is `pendingChecks: true` for ever (util/minimum-release-age.js: no timestamp + required =
pending); and updates/generate.js `generateBranchConfig` REMOVES pending upgrades from a branch
that has non-pending ones ('Branch is not pending, removing pending upgrades'). So the two
halves can only agree when neither waits: github-releases picks the newest release past
3 days, ghcr.io can never pass 3 days. `null` here overrides the 3-day catch-all for BOTH
halves — it MUST live on this rule (the one that groups both) and not on a separate one, or a
later re-grouping inherits the catch-all and re-opens the half-bump; the guard test asserts
both. The trade: uv bumps skip the supply-chain cooldown (feature 034). Accepted because uv is a
CI/build tool whose only merged output — the uv.lock files — still passes every gate, and the
alternative (tracking the image tags via github-releases too) drops the image digests and is
SDD-gated under agents/ and mcp-servers/. Same class as the keycloak (quay.io) and
`docker digest pins` stalls recorded in docs/runbooks/renovate.md §5 — they are NOT fixed here.
Item #308 — give pinDigest its OWN branch, or the initial pin of a tag that also has a
version update is discarded on every run, for ever, and reports nothing.
MEASURED 2026-08-30 with `RENOVATE_PLATFORM=local RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=lookup` over the four app
Dockerfiles. Renovate logged, EIGHT times — once per `python:3.13-slim` reference:
INFO: Ignoring upgrade collision (branch=renovate/docker-base-images)
depName=python currentValue=3.13-slim previousNewValue=3.14-slim thisNewValue=3.13-slim
THE MECHANISM, from renovate@44.52.0's own dist (workers/repository/updates/branchify.js,
branchifyUpgrades): upgrades are de-duplicated PER BRANCH on the key
`${packageFile}:${depName}:${currentValue}`, and a second update for that key with a
different newValue is DROPPED — `logger.info(..., 'Ignoring upgrade collision'); return false`.
The `docker base images` rule above puts every docker update on ONE branch, so the version
update (3.13-slim -> 3.14-slim) and the pinDigest update (3.13-slim -> 3.13-slim@sha256:...)
collide there and the PIN loses.
That is exactly why the 2026-08-30 docker PR added digests to `rust:alpine3.21` and
`ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest` while leaving `python:3.13-slim` bare IN THE SAME FILES: neither
of those tags carries a parseable version, so neither has a competing version update to
collide with. The asymmetry was the tell, and it was not a budget deferral — a deferred
update comes back, and this one could not.
It is INFO, not WARN, and it never reaches the Dependency Dashboard, so this is the §5
'absence reads as health' shape once more: `docker:pinDigests` was in `extends`, doing
nothing for this dep, reporting nothing.
VERIFIED, not assumed: re-running the same lookup with this rule present took the collision
count from EIGHT to ZERO. A separate branch means a separate upgradeKey namespace.
Ordered last so it wins over `docker base images`.
WIDENED TO `digest` 2026-09-04 (item #350). This rule originally separated ONLY the initial pin
and let a digest REFRESH of an already-pinned image ride `docker base images`, reasoning that
splitting routine churn out was pointless. Then `python:3.13-slim` got its pin (feature 063), its
weekly refresh became an updateType `digest`, and the SAME collision came back: the refresh
(3.13-slim -> 3.13-slim@<new digest>) and the version update (3.13-slim -> 3.14-slim) share the
`${packageFile}:${depName}:${currentValue}` key, and the refresh lost — EIGHT times per run,
measured with the same local lookup, while the version update it lost to sat pending. Net
effect: the python base image digest NEVER refreshed, which is the #303 class (advisories a
refresh would clear) reopened for python. A refresh is the one docker update that ALWAYS shares
its key with any version update of the same image, so it needs its own namespace exactly as the
initial pin does. The guard test's control was reversed to assert this.
Item #349 — registries that NEVER supply a release timestamp do not wait for one.
renovate@44's `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour` defaults to `timestamp-required`: with the 3-day
`minimumReleaseAge` above, a release with no `releaseTimestamp` is `pendingChecks` — not for
three days, FOR EVER (util/minimum-release-age.js). The docker datasource has a timestamp ONLY
for Docker Hub (`tag_last_pushed`; its own releaseTimestampNote says so), so every ghcr.io and
quay.io tag, digest and pinDigest is permanently pending. And updates/generate.js
`generateBranchConfig` REMOVES pending upgrades from a branch that holds any ready one
('Branch is not pending, removing pending upgrades'). MEASURED 2026-09-04: `quay.io/keycloak/
keycloak` 26.7.2 -> 26.7.3 dropped from `docker base images` every run — a keycloak security
release would never be proposed, and the dashboard still listed it under Detected Dependencies,
which reads as 'queued'; and the uv image half dropped from `uv pin` (PR #347, fixed on that
rule by removing its cooldown). Waiting on a timestamp a registry cannot supply is not a
cooldown, it is a stall, so these registries run `timestamp-optional`: a release WITH a
timestamp is still aged, one WITHOUT proceeds — the behaviour this config was written against.
DELIBERATELY NOT `matchDatasources: docker` ALONE. Docker Hub tags and digests DO carry
`tag_last_pushed`, so the cooldown there is temporal and real (feature 034's control); widening
this to all of docker would silently disable it for the images it actually works on. The guard
test asserts both halves: ghcr.io/quay.io resolve to timestamp-optional (patch, digest and
pinDigest alike), Docker Hub images resolve to nothing. Add a registry here only after checking
the datasource still cannot time-stamp it. The once-per-run WARN this setting emits is remapped
to info by the top-level `logLevelRemap` — see the note there.
Item #349. Under `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: timestamp-optional` Renovate logs ONCE per run,
at WARN, that some releases had no timestamp. WARNs are what the Dependency Dashboard's
'Repository Problems' section is built from, and renovate-health.mjs (item #311) reads that
section as the channel-death signal. A permanent, EXPECTED warning there is either tuned out —
the failure mode docs/runbooks/renovate.md §5 exists to prevent — or fires the health digest
every week. Renovate 44.46.7's release notes point at this option for exactly this message.
The pattern matches the message, not the whole class: a different WARN still surfaces.
logLevelRemap.matchMessage: /did not have a releaseTimestamp, but as we're running with minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-optional/
